datasets.name: CAD-SEL
datasets.modality: white light colonoscopy and endoscopic ultrasound stills
datasets.citation: Xu et al. 2026, Scientific Data, doi 10.1038/s41597-026-07331-y
datasets.provenance: Six Chinese centres. 5,165 frames of colorectal subepithelial tumours from 641 patients in five classes, imaged with white light endoscopy and endoscopic ultrasound.
datasets.notes: Only the white light images are used. No split is released, so the benchmark tests on the external centres two to six and trains on centre one, which measures transfer across centres. Images are grouped by lesion folder.

datasets.name: EAD2020
datasets.modality: endoscopy video frames from several centres and imaging modalities
datasets.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in the archive and CC BY-NC 3.0 on Mendeley Data, non commercial use only
datasets.citation: Ali et al. 2021, Medical Image Analysis, and Ali et al. 2020, Scientific Reports
datasets.provenance: Training data of the EndoCV2020 artefact detection and segmentation challenge. 2,531 frames with 31,069 boxes of eight artefact classes, and 643 frames with overlapping masks of five artefact classes.
datasets.notes: No official partition exists, since the labels of the challenge test data were never released. Frames of one sequence share a group, while single frames carry no patient identifier and form a group each, so that near duplicate frames of one patient may fall into different partitions. Blood is left out of segmentation, since only 169 of the 643 masks annotate it.

datasets.name: GastroHUN
datasets.citation: Bravo et al. 2025, Scientific Data, doi 10.1038/s41597-025-04401-5
datasets.provenance: Hospital Universitario Nacional de Colombia. 8,834 images of 387 patients, each labelled by four gastroenterologists with one of 22 stations of a systematic stomach screening protocol or an other class.
datasets.notes: Labels are the triple agreement column, the class chosen by at least three of the four annotators, and images without such agreement are excluded. The official patient level test partition is used verbatim.

datasets.name: GastroVision
datasets.provenance: Baerum Hospital, Norway, and Karolinska University Hospital, Sweden. 8,000 images in 27 classes.

overlaps.evidence: byte identical archive members by CRC32 and size, find-those-polyps audit 2026-11-05

datasets.notes: The official split of the authors, published on GitHub (DebeshJha/GastroVision abed639) rather than in the archive, covers the 22 classes evaluated in the paper and leaves out five rare ones. The benchmark adopts its test partition verbatim. Each image forms its own group, since no patient identifiers are released. File names repeat across class folders for different images, so the official lists are matched by folder and name.

datasets.name: HyperKvasir labeled images
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 (competitions and commercial use need permission)
datasets.provenance: Baerum Hospital, Vestre Viken, Norway, 2008 to 2016, Olympus and Pentax endoscopes. 10,662 images in 23 classes, official two fold split.
datasets.notes: The official two fold split assigns every image to fold 0 or 1. The benchmark tests on fold 1, as the split file defines it, and draws validation from fold 0. No patient or video identifiers are released, so each image is its own group and near duplicate frames of one examination may fall on both sides of the split.

datasets.name: Kvasir-Capsule
datasets.provenance: Baerum Hospital, Norway, 2016 to 2018, Olympus EC-S10. 117 videos, 47,238 labeled frames.
datasets.notes: The archive nests one tarball per class, which is streamed and unpacked whole when first used. The official two fold split covers eleven classes, and the benchmark tests on split_1. Frames are grouped by the video identifier in their names, but seven videos occur in both official folds, so the official test partition is not patient disjoint from training. Frames of the videos shared with the official test fold are excluded from training and validation. Angiectasia, Blood, Lymphangiectasia and Ulcer occur in too few videos to appear in validation as well as training, so selection on validation does not see them. The metadata table on OSF adds one axis aligned box to 4,235 finding frames of 21 videos. The detection task keeps the seven box classes present in both official folds, and fresh blood, lymphangiectasia and ulcer come from too few videos to appear in its validation partition.

datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 on OSF, research and education only per the Simula page
datasets.provenance: Baerum Hospital, Vestre Viken, Norway, 2008 to 2016, Olympus and Pentax endoscopes. 590 frames with tools.

overlaps.evidence: byte identical archive members by CRC32 and size, find-those-polyps audit 2026-11-05

datasets.notes: Images and masks are nested tarballs, unpacked whole when first used. The official test list of 118 images is used verbatim, and each image is its own group.

datasets.name: Kvasir-SEG
datasets.provenance: Baerum Hospital, Vestre Viken, Norway, 2008 to 2016, Olympus and Pentax endoscopes. 1,000 polyp images with masks, the polyp class of Kvasir v2.
datasets.notes: The PraNet split (Fan et al. 2020) tests on 100 images, but its file list is only distributed inside archives that also carry data under a separate agreement. The benchmark therefore holds out a seeded fifth of the images. Without patient identifiers each image is its own group. The checksum was computed by the benchmark at registration, since none is published.

datasets.notes: No official split is released. The benchmark holds out a stratified fifth of the images, each image forming its own group.

datasets.name: LIMUC
datasets.citation: Polat et al., LIMUC dataset, Zenodo 2022
datasets.provenance: Marmara University, Istanbul, Turkiye, December 2011 to July 2019. 11,276 images, 564 patients, 1,043 colonoscopies.
datasets.notes: Official test set of 1,686 images. Train and validation are split by patient. The archive files 10 byte identical images under two different Mayo scores (for instance UC_patient_130_20 under Mayo 2 and Mayo 3). These contradictory images are excluded, which leaves 1,682 test images.

datasets.name: Nerthus
datasets.licence: no licence stated, released by Simula for research
datasets.provenance: Baerum Hospital, Vestre Viken, Norway, 2008 to 2016, Olympus and Pentax endoscopes. 21 videos, 5,525 frames with Boston bowel preparation scores.
datasets.notes: Frames are named bowel_<video>_score_<score>-<n>_<frame>, and every video carries one Boston bowel preparation score. Splits group frames by video, so the test partition holds only a few of the 21 videos and scores vary accordingly. Only two videos carry score 0, so validation has none while training and test have one each.

datasets.name: PolypDB
datasets.modality: WLI, NBI, LCI, BLI and FICE stills
datasets.licence: research and education use per the authors, no formal licence on OSF
datasets.provenance: Baerum (Norway), Karolinska (Sweden) and Hanoi (Vietnam). 3,934 images with masks.

overlaps.note: all 2,588 WLI and 136 NBI images of centre C1
overlaps.name: HyperKvasir unlabeled images

datasets.notes: Tasks follow the official modality wise test partitions of the authors' repository. Validation is drawn by the benchmark from the remaining images. Hanoi images are grouped by the patient code in their file names. The BLI, LCI and FICE test partitions hold fewer than ten images, so their scores carry large uncertainty.

datasets.name: WCEBleedGen
datasets.provenance: 1,309 bleeding frames with masks and boxes and 1,309 non bleeding frames, compiled from several sources described only as internet sources, without patient identifiers.
datasets.notes: No split or patient identifiers are released, so each frame is its own group and near duplicate frames may cross the benchmark split. Its sources are not documented, so overlap with other capsule datasets cannot be excluded.
